question: At identical per-trigger maximum output-token budget, does a single reasoning resample outperform repeated independent nonthinking samples?
alternative_explanation: Original reasoning benefit may reflect more generation budget rather than uniquely informative reasoning content.
independent_unit: Task, not sample;14 treated pairs,100 full-cohort denominator
reasoning: One call; T0.6,p0.95,k20,thinking enabled; stop at EOS or2048. Index4.
nonthinking: Repeated calls from original prompt, T0.7,p0.8,k20; cap=min(768,remaining); debit actual output tokens including special/partial tokens; no visible-test early stopping. Indices5 onward.
seed_rule: sha256(matched:20260915:{task_id}:{reasoning|nonthinking}:{zero_based_arm_call})[:8] as hex; all calls newly generated
selection: For each arm choose candidate with most public assertions passed; earliest sample_index breaks ties. Replace baseline only on strictly more passed assertions; otherwise baseline fallback. Selection before hidden scoring; no hidden oracle.
primary_development_contrast: Final selected-answer accuracy reasoning minus nonthinking over100 tasks; report paired wins/losses and task-bootstrap uncertainty; underpowered conclusions qualified.
secondary: Completion/parseability, all token and call costs, latency with desktop caveats, trigger-level rescues/regressions. Equal output-budget ceilings are not equal actual tokens or FLOPs; report remaining unused reasoning allowance.
failure_policy: Retain malformed,empty,partial attempts; no quality retry. Resume exact saved keys. Zero-token generation stops as operational failure, not infinite retry.
model: Existing fingerprinted Qwen3-4B BF16;9216MiB free guard
selection_implementation_status: Rule frozen; isolated selector/scoring adapter still to implement before hidden scoring
protected: No reserve or external holdout; old180 confirmation not used.
